reverse_outline.summary: What the part covers: the marketplace as a business before software
Business stakes: model sets charges, risks and regulators; liquidity drives renewals and returns
Architects' stake: later boundaries and platform decisions are justified by this part
Key points: model as per-country/category configuration / liquidity per cell as requirements / mapping capabilities before sharing decisions
Failure patterns the part counters: vanity liquidity, forced fit, deal-shaped architecture
Why the book starts with the business: the business model dictates the architecture
Three kinds of business knowledge needed to decide sharing: marketplace type and liquidity, industry history, capabilities and boundaries
Roadmap: six chapters as six questions grouped into model, history and what the marketplace does
Table of chapter questions and when to read each
The part's vocabulary and how it links to the Preface and later parts
Veldmark's chief architect applies each chapter's tool: profiles, liquidity cells, history, capability map, contexts, share test
Closing: the chapters set constraints for later design; start with the marketplace taxonomy chapter

results.finding: Both flow readers had to re-read this bullet to work out what is inside and outside the five overlaps: it nests three counts in one sentence. A split (five overlaps; separately, the Poland overlap and one deliberate duplicate) would keep the facts and the order.
